speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how far along you are in your pregnancy and when the bleeding and abdominal pain started? Also, is the bleeding heavy or just light spotting?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a prior cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe pain with bleeding, I need to know if you have any tearing or ripping sensations in your abdomen. Do you feel the baby moving normally, or have you noticed any decrease in fetal movement?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Do you feel a tearing or ripping sensation in your abdomen, and have you noticed any decrease in fetal movement? Also, are you currently experiencing dizziness or feeling faint?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: One previous childbirth via cesarean section. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol consumption. Works as an elementary school teacher.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis: Findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum. Vital Signs: Pulse 110/min, Blood Pressure 90/60 mm Hg, Respiratory Rate 17/min. Obstetric Exam: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring shows recurrent variable decelerations; no contractions felt. Abdominal Exam: Mild distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound predominating, diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Hematology: Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL (decreased), Platelets 200,000 /μL. Coagulation: PT 11 seconds, aPTT 30 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms a uterine rupture with internal bleeding, and your vitals show you are already in shock. This is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgery to save both you and the baby. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
